help.score_water: Water: how much of the crops' water need the rain in their season covers. Higher = less irrigation.
help.score_soil: Soil: legumes that add nitrogen, deep and shallow roots in turn, and cover crops. Higher = healthier soil.
help.score_erosion: Erosion: how little bare soil the stormy months see. Higher = less soil washed away.
help.score_pest: Pests: different plant families in turn break pest and disease cycles. Higher = fewer problems.
help.score_climate: Climate: heat days, late frost and season length for each crop here. Higher = better suited.
help.score_income: Income: local yield × ZPIS price, compared with the best rotation. Gross, before costs.
help.confidence: Confidence: how sure Niva is. It drops when a price or yield is missing, or the field is far from our data points.
help.whatIf: Try a drier or hotter future: Niva scores every rotation again with less rain or more heat.
help.et0: ET₀: how much water a short green crop would use in a day, from heat and sun (FAO-56 formula).
help.heatDays: Heat days: days in June–August above 35 °C. Maize and peppers suffer; sorghum copes.
help.frostFree: Frost-free season: from the last spring frost to the first autumn frost (minimum at or below 0 °C).
help.forecastError: On 2023–2024, years the model never saw, its forecast was off by this much on average. Guessing "no change" was off by the second number.
help.gwet: NASA POWER GWETTOP and GWETROOT: the share of the soil's pores filled with water, at the top and in the root zone (~50 km grid). Below about 35% the seedbed is dry; above about 80% the soil is too wet to work.
help.eta: ET₀ is how much water the weather pulls from a reference grass field. ETa = ET₀ × Kc is what your crop uses at its growth stage (FAO-56). Rain minus ETa tells you if the field gained or lost water.
help.ndvi: NDVI from NASA MODIS (250 m): 0 is bare soil, about 0.3 sparse plants, 0.6+ a dense green crop. Comparing with the same weeks in earlier years shows if the crop is behind.
help.soilProfile: ISRIC SoilGrids 2.0 (250 m map). Clay holds water and nutrients; sand drains fast. pH 6–7.5 suits most crops. SOC = soil organic carbon. CEC = how much nutrient the soil can hold.
help.sprayWindow: A good day to spray: wind under 20 km/h, no rain that day and under 2 mm the next, below 30 °C. Forecast from Open-Meteo.
help.soldMissing: Nobody publishes how many tonnes were actually sold or bought out per region (MakStat and ZPIS do not). We leave it empty instead of guessing.
help.layer_smap: NASA SMAP L4: soil moisture in the top 5 cm, about 9 km squares. Blue = wet, brown = dry.
help.layer_ndvi: NASA MODIS NDVI, 8-day: how green the land is. Dark green = dense crops or forest.
help.layer_lst: NASA MODIS land surface temperature by day: hot spots show dry or bare ground.
help.layer_rain: NASA GPM IMERG: rain falling, from satellites, about 10 km squares.
